stem: A nurse is planning mental health care for a client whose cultural health beliefs differ from the nurse's own. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Use the nurse's own explanatory model consistently so treatment decisions are not influenced by different cultural beliefs
options.B: Ask about the client's individual health beliefs, values, preferences, and communication needs and provide respectful care that responds to them when clinically feasible
options.C: Assume clients from the same cultural group share the same beliefs and select care based on expected group preferences
options.D: Avoid discussing cultural beliefs because high-quality mental health care should exclude personal explanatory models

rationale: The HHS National CLAS Standards call for effective, understandable, respectful quality care that responds to cultural health beliefs and practices, language, health literacy, and communication needs. HHS nursing CLAS training further emphasizes understanding and responding to each patient's experiences, values, beliefs, and preferences while addressing bias and stereotypes. B is correct because it individualizes culturally responsive care rather than imposing the clinician's beliefs or stereotyping the client by group membership.
educational_objective: Provide individualized, culturally and linguistically responsive mental health care without stereotyping or imposing the nurse's own explanatory model.
source_organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Minority Health / Think Cultural Health
source_document_title: National Standards for Culturally and Linguistically Appropriate Services (CLAS) in Health and Health Care; CLAS in Nursing
source_version_date: Current HHS CLAS standards and nursing program accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: National CLAS Standards — Principal Standard 1; CLAS in Nursing — program focus on understanding, respecting, and responding to patient experiences, values, beliefs, and preferences and awareness of bias/stereotypes
source_claim_supported: Culturally responsive care should be respectful and responsive to each patient's cultural health beliefs/practices and communication needs, with individualized attention to experiences, values, beliefs, and preferences rather than stereotypes.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity — cultural influences on health, therapeutic relationships, client-centered psychosocial care
blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — culturally responsive mental health care

source_original.stem: A nurse is providing mental health care to a client whose cultural background has different beliefs about mental illness than the nurse's own, and the nurse initially wonders whether it would be simpler to just apply their own clinical framework rather than navigate the difference. Culturally sensitive care instead includes:

options.A: Use the nurse's own explanatory model consistently so treatment decisions are not altered by differing cultural beliefs about mental illness.
options.B: Explore the client's beliefs and preferences, incorporate them into collaborative care when feasible, and avoid stereotyping the individual.
options.C: Assume clients from the same cultural group share the same beliefs, then select treatment according to the group's expected preferences.
options.D: Avoid discussing cultural beliefs because biomedical treatment is most effective when personal explanatory models are excluded from care.

source_original.rationale: Culturally sensitive mental health care includes understanding and respecting the client's own cultural beliefs about mental illness, its causes, and appropriate treatment approaches (which may differ significantly across cultures), integrating this understanding into a collaborative, individualized care approach — while also recognizing individual variation within any cultural group rather than assuming uniformity.
source_original.source_detail: National CLAS Standards, Principal Standard: respectful, understandable, quality care responsive to cultural health beliefs/practices, preferred languages, health literacy, and other communication needs. Current HHS Think Cultural Health standards reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Corrected the source identity from APA to HHS Office of Minority Health/Think Cultural Health, removed the stem's cueing narrative, and rewrote the keyed response to match the CLAS Principal Standard and current CLAS-in-Nursing emphasis on individual values, beliefs, preferences, and anti-stereotyping. Difficulty reduced from hard to medium.

audit_findings.source_authority: Official HHS Office of Minority Health CLAS standards and nursing program; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: Current HHS Think Cultural Health standards/nursing pages checked 2026-08-17.
audit_findings.claim_audit: HHS Principal Standard directly requires respectful care responsive to cultural health beliefs/practices and communication needs; HHS nursing program emphasizes experiences, values, beliefs, preferences, bias, and stereotypes.

distractor_audit.A: Imposes the clinician's explanatory model rather than responding to the client.
distractor_audit.C: Uses stereotyping/group assumptions rather than individual assessment.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: B is uniquely compatible with CLAS and individualized care; 'when clinically feasible' prevents cultural preference from being treated as overriding safety/standards.
audit_findings.cueing: Removed the original nurse-thought narrative and shortened alternatives.
audit_findings.blueprint: Cultural influences and therapeutic psychosocial care fit Psychosocial Integrity.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked HHS CLAS Principal Standard and CLAS-in-Nursing overview; B remains uniquely correct.
